name: phd-35-allowance-priority
description: §3.5 allows one or two 6xxxx courses from the junior/senior year, and this 4+1 student took four of them. The allowance is six credits, so two transfer — and the DGS chose which two (2026-09-10): 'prioritize courses that can satisfy the qualifier examination requirements (both core knowledge requirement and specialization category requirement). Among the courses that satisfy the qualifier examination requirements, prioritize the courses that will satisfy more requirements.' CSE 60641 and CSE 60111 carry both a §4.4.1 core area and a §4.4.2 group, so they fill it; CSE 60770 (a group only) and CSE 60999 (neither) fall outside it. The two that fall outside still earn nothing else — an over-allowance course is over it whatever else it might have done.

detailIncludes: 6 of the 6 credits from before your bachelor’s degree used
